source_text: Conuersus ibidem ad discipulos (uae\' dicit auctori scan. dalorum: expedisse ei, si natus non fuisset aut si molino saxo ad collum deligato praecipitatus esset in profundum, quam unum ex illis modicis utique discipulis eius scandalizasset. aestima, quale supplicium comminetur ille. nec enim! alius ulciscetur scandalum discipulorum eius. agnosce igitur et iudicem et illo adfectu pronuntiantem de cura suorum, quo et creator retro: qui tetigerit uos, ac si pupillam oculi mei tangat. idem sensus eiusdem est. peccantem fratrem iubet corripi; quod qui non fecerit, utique deliquit, aut ex odio uolens fratrem in delicto perseuerare aut ex acceptione personae parcens ei: habes Leuiticum: non odies fratrem tuum in animo tuo, traductione traduces proximum tuum, utique et fratrem, et non sumes propter illum delictum. nec mirum, si ita docet qui pecora quoque fratris tui, si errantia in uia inueneris, prohibet despicias, quominus ea reducas fratri, nedum ipsum sibi. sed et ueniam des fratri in te delinquenti iubet, etiam septies. parum plane. plus est enim apud creatorem, qui nec modum statuit, in infinitum pronuntians: fratris malitiae memor ne sis, nec petenti eam praestes mandat, sed et non petenti. non enim dones offensam uult, sed obliuiscaris. Lex leprosorum quantae sit interpretationis erga species ipsius uitii et inspectationis summi sacerdotis, nostrum erit scire, Marcionis, morositatem legis opponere, ut et hic Christum aemulum eius adfirmet, praeuenientem sollemnia legis etiam in curatione decem leprosorum, quos tantummodo ire iussos, ut se ostenderent sacerdotibus, in itinere purgauit, sine tactu iam et sine uerbo, tacita potestate et sola uoluntate.
pass_a_gloss: Having turned there to the disciples, He says to the author of scandals: it would have been better for him if he had not been born or if, with a millstone of rock having been tied around his neck, he had been thrown into the deep, than that he scandalized one of those little disciples of His. Estimate what kind of punishment He threatens. For no other will avenge the scandal of His disciples. Recognize, therefore, both the judge and the one pronouncing about the care of His own, with that same affection with which the Creator formerly: whoever touches you, touches, as it were, the pupil of my eye. The same sense is His. He commands to rebuke a sinning brother; which whoever does not do, certainly has failed, either from hatred, willing that the brother persist in the sin, or from partiality, sparing him. You have Leviticus: you shall not hate your brother in your heart, you shall surely rebuke your neighbor, certainly also your brother, and you shall not bear sin on his account. Nor is it wonderful, if He teaches thus, who also forbids that you despise the livestock of your brother, if you find them straying in the way, so that you may lead them back to your brother, and not just that. But He also commands that you forgive a brother who sins against you, even seven times. Plainly, it is not enough. For it is more with the Creator, who does not set a limit, pronouncing to infinity: be not mindful of your brother's malice, and do not grant it to one who asks, but also to one who does not ask. For He does not want you to give offense, but to forget. The law of lepers, how great an interpretation it is with respect to the species of that vice and the inspection of the high priest, will be ours to know, Marcion, to oppose the morosity of the law, so that even here Christ may be affirmed as the rival of the latter, anticipating the solemnities of the law even in the healing of the ten lepers, whom, having been commanded only to go and show themselves to the priests, He purified on the way, without touch and without word, with silent power and sole will.

pass_b_english: He turns to the disciples and says to the author of scandals: it would have been better for him if he had never been born, or if a millstone had been hung around his neck and he had been thrown into the depths, than to scandalize one of these little disciples of His. Calculate what kind of punishment He threatens. No one else will avenge the scandal of His disciples. Recognize, therefore, both the Judge and the One who speaks with that same affection for His own with which the Creator once spoke: "Whoever touches you touches the pupil of My eye" (Zechariah 2:8). It is the same mind. He commands that a sinning brother be rebuked; whoever fails to do so has certainly sinned, either from hatred, wanting the brother to persist in the fault, or from partiality, sparing him. You have Leviticus: "You shall not hate your brother in your heart; you shall surely rebuke your neighbor" — certainly your brother as well — "and you shall not bear sin because of him" (Leviticus 19:17). Nor is it surprising that He teaches this way, since He also forbids you to ignore your brother's livestock if you find them straying on the road, so that you may bring them back to your brother — and not only the animals. But He also commands you to forgive a brother who sins against you, even seven times. Clearly, that is not enough. For there is more with the Creator, who sets no limit but declares it to infinity: do not hold your brother's malice in mind, and grant forgiveness not only to the one who asks but also to the one who does not ask. For He does not want you to give offense, but to forget. The law of lepers — how great its interpretation is regarding the very nature of that vice and the inspection of the high priest — will be ours to know, Marcion, so that we may oppose the moroseness of the law, and so that even here Christ may be affirmed as its rival, anticipating the law's solemnities even in the healing of the ten lepers. He commanded them only to go show themselves to the priests, and He purified them on the way, without touch and without a word, by silent power and sheer will.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a literal gloss, and Pass B provides a fluent translation with necessary scripture identifications (Zechariah 2:8 and Leviticus 19:17) which were alluded to in the Latin. The distinction between the Creator's affection and the Judge's pronouncement is preserved. The complex sentence regarding the law of lepers is handled correctly in both versions.
